name: /health returns 200 before the model is loaded, so a liveness-style readiness probe routes traffic to a replica that will fail every request for minutes
symptom: After a rollout, a fraction of requests fail with connection errors or immediate 500s against newly-created pods that Kubernetes reports as Ready. The failure window is the model load time and it varies per pod, so the error rate looks stochastic. Meanwhile the pods are Ready by every probe vLLM's default docs suggest, and CPU and memory look normal because the process is alive and doing nothing.
root_cause: There are three distinct lifecycle states — Container Running, API Server Ready, and Model Loaded — and vLLM's /health endpoint only reports the middle one. llm-d's readiness guide is explicit: 'The vLLM /health endpoint only indicates that the server process is running, not that models are loaded and ready to serve.' /health returns 200 as soon as the server process starts and does not wait for model loading; /v1/models returns 503 or connection-refused during loading and 200 with model metadata once ready. Because Kubernetes endpoint removal and InferencePool membership are readiness-driven ('as their readiness state changes, the EPP automatically updates its internal list of healthy candidates'), a wrong readiness definition propagates directly into routing decisions. TGI has the same shape of problem and its own solution to point at: a health() method with start_health() defaulting to false, commented 'Typically false, or true if the backend includes a warmup phase', plus /health returning 503 {"error":"unhealthy","error_type":"healthcheck"}.
workaround: Use /health for liveness only and /v1/models for both startupProbe and readinessProbe, which is llm-d's recommended shape. Size the startupProbe to the actual load time: their worked example is failureThreshold 60 at periodSeconds 30, which they compute as a 30-minute maximum startup time, and the failure modes they list include 'Model download taking longer than the failureThreshold allows'. Match the probe port to the pod's role — prefill 8000, decode 8200 through a sidecar, standalone 8000 — since a port mismatch looks exactly like a pod that never becomes ready. Eliminate the variable rather than tuning it: pre-download weights with an init container or a persistent volume, mount a torch-compile cache (llm-d reports this plus a fast startupProbe taking pod-ready time from ~2m15s to ~100s), and note that some engines will not even accept a request until weights are present (SGLang has --checkpoint-engine-wait-weights-before-ready for exactly this class of problem).
notes: There is no first-class fix: vLLM has no dedicated model-aware readiness endpoint, and the reason is a tracked open request (vLLM #6073). Using /v1/models as the readiness probe is the current best practice precisely because it is a workaround for a missing endpoint, which means the probe's semantics are incidental — a future change to that endpoint's behaviour would silently change traffic routing. Record it as an open design gap, not a settled pattern. SCHEME RECLASSIFIED (2026-10-04): was 'config'.
